items.message: Fresh-verdict filter uses a string key `{case}/{arm}` that differs from what `Verdict` likely uses as its replay key.
`_ensure_judge_bound` binds `AiJudge` silently when no route is declared, but `AiJudge` refuses an unrouted call — so the auto-bind saves no refusal, only buries the error later.

`_sidecar_for` falls back to `corpus / f"{case}{SIDECAR_SUFFIX}"` for an unknown case, but the gate says a verdict paid for must not be lost — a renamed case would silently miss the fallback sidecar on replay.
medium: <!-- guardrail: baseline -->
medium: <!-- skill: review/review-format -->
`_sidecar_for` scans the full corpus with `load_cases` to locate one case by name.
`_corpus_rubrics` and `_judged` each call `load_cases(corpus)`, and `_known_verdicts` does a separate `rglob` — three directory scans per `judge_corpus` invocation.
medium: <!-- guardrail: baseline -->
medium: <!-- skill: review/review-format -->
Case `name` from corpus JSON used to construct sidecar path without containment check.
Sidecar glob reads all `*.verdicts.jsonl` files recursively; a symlink or planted file outside normal case directories is silently ingested.
medium: <!-- guardrail: baseline -->
medium: <!-- skill: review/review-format -->

Pass-rate assertion is wrong for the corpus test: 2/3 requires `broken` to count as a decided failure, but `broken`'s deterministic check fails against the *recorded* answer, meaning whether `_decided` now treats it as failed matters.
`again.value.after.judged == 1` asserts replay produced a judged count, but does not assert the verdict *value* (level) that was replayed.
`sink.append_text` is called with a concatenated string of all verdicts for a case; if a partial write fails mid-string, no verdict in that batch is recoverable.
